page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left page: a list of numbered theses at the top, a horizontal rule, then a centred title "Octavæ Prælectionis Summarium." with a numbered list below. Right page: only a narrow cropped strip at the right edge, showing fragments of its left margin numerals and a large letter "N". Nothing else from the right page is legible.

main_text.l: Dubium Secundum. An ut Leges ob-ligent, populi aliquis saltem consensus requiratur ?
17. &c. In Principe constituendo quæ sint populi partes.
21. Potestatem, (dato quòd esset Principi à populo delata,) populus resumendi jus non habet.
22. &c. Unde fiat, ut ad Legis Obligationem populi consensus aliquis putetur esse necessarius.
25. &c. Dubium Tertium. Qualis quantusque populi consensus requiratur ?
28. Dubium Quartum. De Legibus minorum Communitatum.

page.notes: The "P" at the start of "Propositio" is a large drop initial, read as P. The right-hand printed page is cropped to a narrow strip; its margin numerals (10, 7, 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 24, 25 and 1, 2, 4, 9, 12, 15) and the large "N" heading are only partly visible and are not transcribed. Show-through from the reverse side is ignored. The word "Rejecto" is read with a long-s-free spelling as printed; the "fig-/mento" and "ob-/ligent" and "Summa-/rium" splits are printed line-end hyphens.
